sections.title: One noun, three questions
sections.content: You now know all three members of this set: -nál/-nél ("at"), -hoz/-hez/-höz ("to"), and -tól/-től ("from"). They answer three different questions about the same place — Hol vagy? ("Where are you?"), Hová mész? ("Where are you going?"), Honnan jössz? ("Where are you coming from?") — and none of them can substitute for another.

items.english: Where are you? I'm at the bakery.
Where are you going? I'm going to the bakery.

sections.content: Honnan jössz? A pékségtől jövök completes the set — "Where are you coming from? I'm coming from the bakery." All three suffixes follow the same vowel harmony you already use everywhere: whatever ending -nál/-nél needs, -hoz/-hez/-höz and -tól/-től need the matching one.
